root.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Romanishin Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. g3

overview: White fianchettoes the king's bishop against the Nimzo-Indian pin. In the main line Black strikes with ...c5, and after Nf3 cxd4 Nxd4 O-O Bg2 the position is an open-Sicilian-style fight against a Maroczy-like White set-up. White keeps the centre solid and presses with Bg2 and Qd3; Black develops with ...Nc6 and ...d5 or ...b6.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto on g2 and pressure d5 and the long diagonal
Recapture on d4 with a knight and play Qd3 or Bd2
Keep c4 and e2 to restrain ...d5

black_ideas.idea: Play ...c5 and trade on d4 for counterplay

typical_structures.structure: Symmetrical c4/e2 against ...e6/...d6-type Black set-up after ...cxd4 Nxd4
Doubled c-pawns if Black takes on c3

character.notes: Play after 4...c5 5.Nf3 cxd4 6.Nxd4 O-O 7.Bg2 is equal and strategic without forced lines.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: A respected alternative to 4.e3 and 4.Qc2 with no real risk.

structure.notes: The d-pawns trade on d4 and the c-file is half-open, as in an open Sicilian.

approach.notes: A mainstream line in the Nimzo-Indian, played by Kasparov and Romanishin.

level.notes: Plans are positional and need good piece placement, with modest theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Delayed fianchetto
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Nf3 c5 5. g3
sublines_that_differ.how: White first plays Nf3 and then g3, reaching the same ideas.
